sections.overview: Carukia barnesi is a small box jellyfish from northern Australian waters and the first species linked to Irukandji syndrome.
sections.identification: Its transparent bell is about 1–2 cm across, while its tentacles can reach roughly 1 m; small size makes it difficult to see in water.
sections.habitat: It is usually solitary offshore in northern Australia, from Western Australia to Queensland, and winds and currents sometimes carry it inshore.
sections.diet: Immature medusae feed on invertebrate prey, while mature medusae shift toward vertebrate prey, according to a species-specific study.
sections.behavior: Most aspects of its behavior remain little known; prey capture appears to change as the animal matures.
sections.reproduction: Its life cycle includes fertilized eggs, a planula stage, polyps that reproduce by budding, and medusae released by strobilation.
sections.ecology: The common label “Irukandji” also refers to other small box jellies, including Malo kingi; C. barnesi is one species within this broader group.
sections.conservation: Its sting can cause Irukandji syndrome, a potentially severe illness; species-level abundance and conservation status are not well assessed.
